expectations.text: Correctly detects entry state A (profile only, no proposed endeavor) and runs Step 0 endeavor proposal.
expectations.evidence: No entry-state detection. Proceeds to discuss what an endeavor is and offers framings but also gives a verdict.

expectations.text: Does NOT silently pick a candidate and barrel into evaluation; ends with explicit user-selection question.
expectations.evidence: Recommends Option B and then proceeds to give viability assessment for all three prongs without waiting for user confirmation.

expectations.text: Proposes 3-5 differentiated candidates along strategically meaningful axes.
expectations.evidence: Three candidates (Options A, B, C) but they are along a single axis (narrow-to-broad). Not differentiated by strategic axis (deployment vs. methods vs. benchmark).

expectations.text: Each candidate is Specific (clears the field-vs-endeavor rule).
expectations.evidence: Option A and B remain theme-level ('AI-driven drug discovery applications to U.S. biotech'). Only the example reframe is Specific.

expectations.text: Each candidate is grounded in documented anchor facts (no hallucinated relationships or PI-track positions claimed today).
expectations.evidence: Baseline grounds suggestions in profile facts and is honest about gaps.

expectations.text: Marks a recommended starting point with rationale (or honest neutrality if candidates are close).
expectations.evidence: Recommends Option B with rationale ('most flexibility without sacrificing credibility').

expectations.text: Cites Dhanasar at 889 inline when discussing field-vs-endeavor reasoning.
expectations.evidence: References Dhanasar by name; does not pinpoint to 889. Does not cite the 2024 USCIS policy update precisely either.

expectations.text: Notes EB-2 baseline is satisfied (U.S. Ph.D.) and does not unnecessarily run Step 0.5.
expectations.evidence: Notes 'M.S. in CS from a U.S. R1.' meets EB-2 base requirement. Does not unnecessarily flag baseline.

expectations.text: Mentions priority-date backlog as relevant context (does not require AC21 framing for academic postdoc, but should flag if country of birth unknown).
expectations.evidence: Does not surface backlog context. (Baseline is not designed to be sensitive to this.)

expectations.text: Applies ESL-professional writing style.
expectations.evidence: Reasonable structure but uses some idioms: 'rule of thumb,' 'load-bearing document,' 'cheap insurance.' ESL accessibility moderate.

expectations.text: Correctly detects entry state 0.5 (EB-2 baseline at risk) and runs Step 0.5 instead of full Dhanasar evaluation.
expectations.evidence: Lines 17-39: opens with EB-2 threshold issue and explicitly says 'Resolve the credential evaluation question first. Everything below is moot if you cannot establish EB-2 eligibility.' Strong baseline-check identification.

expectations.text: Cites 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(k)(2) for advanced-degree requirement.
expectations.evidence: References '4-year U.S. bachelor's' rule but does not pinpoint to 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(k)(2).

expectations.text: Cites Matter of Katigbak for specialty-alignment rule.
expectations.evidence: Does not cite Matter of Katigbak. Mentions specialty alignment loosely but without precedent anchor.

expectations.text: Cites USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 6 Pt. F Ch. 5(D)(1) for the eligibility framework.
expectations.evidence: References 'USCIS and the Department of State have historically treated' without Policy Manual pinpoint.

expectations.text: Identifies the foreign three-year bachelor's without credential evaluation as the central issue.
expectations.evidence: Line 25: '3-year Indian B.Com. as not equivalent to a U.S. four-year bachelor's degree for EB-2 purposes.' Correctly identifies the central issue.

expectations.text: Identifies specialty-alignment issue (B.Com. vs. product management) per Katigbak.
expectations.evidence: Does not raise specialty-alignment issue between Commerce degree and product management. Misses this Katigbak point.

expectations.text: Walks through Route 2 (exceptional ability) as an alternative, including the 6-category test.
expectations.evidence: Lines 31-39: covers exceptional ability route at high level. Does not enumerate all six categories systematically.

expectations.text: Asks targeted clarifying questions (credential evaluation? exceptional ability route? specialty alignment?).
expectations.evidence: Lists action items but does not pose targeted questions for user to answer.

expectations.text: Does NOT run the Dhanasar three-prong analysis.
expectations.evidence: Proceeds to a full Dhanasar Prong 1/2/3 analysis after the baseline check ('assuming you clear EB-2 baseline').

expectations.text: Tone is honest but not catastrophizing.
expectations.evidence: Direct and honest. Notes 'real risk of denial' but pairs with concrete remediation steps.

expectations.text: Suggests credential evaluation services as concrete next step.
expectations.evidence: Line 111: 'Credential evaluation of your B.Com. by WES/ECE/SpanTran. Do this first.' Concrete next step.

expectations.text: Applies ESL-professional writing style.
expectations.evidence: Mixed. Uses some idioms ('plan B,' 'cheap insurance') and informal terms. Some technical terms not explained for ESL ('AC21 §104(c)' mentioned without gloss).

expectations.text: Correctly identifies entry state C and runs Step 0b reframing before full evaluation.
expectations.evidence: Proceeds directly to full Prong 1/2/3 evaluation with verdict.

expectations.text: Flags market-size framing as insufficient under USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 6 Pt. F Ch. 5(D)(6) for entrepreneurs.
expectations.evidence: Line 26: 'Multi-billion-dollar market framing is a known weak argument. Matter of Dhanasar and the Policy Manual are explicit that market size alone does not establish national importance.' Less pinpoint than with_skill but flags the issue.

expectations.text: Applies founder/entrepreneur archetype calibration correctly.
expectations.evidence: Has a scoring table mapped against the 2022 Policy Manual entrepreneur evidence list. Applies entrepreneur framework, though without explicit (D)(6) pinpoint.

expectations.text: Includes at-a-glance summary at top of memo showing current verdict and achievable ceiling.
expectations.evidence: No at-a-glance table. Memo opens with TLDR but does not separate current state from achievable ceiling in structured format.

expectations.text: Proposes 2-3 narrower candidate framings grounded in record (FDA pathway, named pilot, LOIs).
expectations.evidence: Recommends rewriting the endeavor but does not present multiple differentiated candidate framings for selection.

expectations.text: Names honest weaknesses (pre-clearance, conditional LOIs, modest citations, interested-party recommenders).
expectations.evidence: Lines 47-56: identifies 'mostly interested parties' recommender problem, 'no FDA clearance,' 'no revenue,' 'university-assigned patent.' Honest.

expectations.text: Stops at the explicit user-selection question.
expectations.evidence: Proceeds to a full evaluation and now-vs-wait guidance without offering candidate framings for selection.

expectations.text: Does NOT invent numerical probability estimates of approval.
expectations.evidence: Baseline avoids probability estimates here. Uses 'plausible / weak / moderate' qualitative terms.

expectations.text: Surfaces backlog reality but does not lead with it as a discouragement.
expectations.evidence: Lines 111: 'Country-of-chargeability and concurrent I-485 strategy materially affect the cost/benefit of timing — they are outside this memo's scope.' Mentioned but not centered.

expectations.text: Applies ESL-professional writing style.
expectations.evidence: Some idioms: 'Bottom line up front (BLUF),' 'plan and budget,' 'plays it safe.' ESL accessibility moderate.

expectations.text: Correctly identifies entry state C and runs Step 0b reframing.
expectations.evidence: No entry-state detection. Proceeds directly to a full Prong 1/2/3 memo with verdict.

expectations.text: Cites Dhanasar at 889 for field-vs-endeavor; identifies the employer-only-impact pattern as a Prong 1 risk.
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'theme, not an endeavor' and 'captive impact' but without pinpoint Dhanasar citations.

expectations.text: Applies industry-archetype evidence calibration (does not penalize for absence of publications).
expectations.evidence: Recognizes industry profile in evaluation; does not require academic publications. Mentions patents filed are valuable even if not granted.

expectations.text: Proposes 3 narrower candidate restatements differentiated along strategic axes.
expectations.evidence: Suggests a single reframe and lists 'concrete next steps' but does not present multiple differentiated candidates for selection.

expectations.text: Does not invent numerical probability estimates of approval.
expectations.evidence: Hallucinated probabilities: 'Approval without RFE: unlikely (~15-25%)', 'plausible (~35-45%)', 'meaningful risk (~30-40%).'

expectations.text: Stops at the explicit user-selection question and does not simulate the user's answer.
expectations.evidence: Proceeds to a full evaluation with prong-by-prong analysis and 6-step pre-filing action list without offering candidate framings to select among.

expectations.text: Cites USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 6 Pt. F Ch. 5 for relevant rules (D(1) baseline, D(3) sub-factors, D(4) credentials-not-sufficient).
expectations.evidence: References '2022 USCIS policy update' loosely. Does not pinpoint Policy Manual sections.

expectations.text: Identifies recommender-pool independence weakness.
expectations.evidence: Line 48: 'recommendation letters from your own manager and skip-level will be heavily discounted as non-independent.' Identifies the issue.

expectations.text: Does NOT use credentials as Prong 1 evidence (maintains Prong 1 / Prong 2 separation).
expectations.evidence: Generally maintains the separation; discusses Prong 2 strengths separately. Some minor blending in framing language but not a category error.

expectations.text: Applies ESL-professional writing style.
expectations.evidence: Idioms and casual phrasing: 'coin flip with RFE risk,' 'budget for an RFE response,' 'puffery,' 'plan and budget for an RFE response.' Some terms used without inline gloss for ESL readers.

expectations.text: Correctly detects entry state 0 (orientation needed) and runs Step 0.0 orientation instead of full evaluation.
expectations.evidence: No entry-state detection but does correctly recognize the user is unfamiliar and provides orientation-style content. Distinction is methodological.

expectations.text: Explains what NIW is in plain language (waiver of job offer + labor cert within EB-2).
expectations.evidence: Lines 9-23: extensive explanation of what NIW is, EB-2 placement, self-petition, PERM skip. Thorough.

expectations.text: Covers the three Dhanasar prongs in plain language.
expectations.evidence: Lines 33-44: three prongs covered with examples. Good plain-language explanation.

expectations.text: Distinguishes 'proposed endeavor' from 'endeavor statement.'
expectations.evidence: Does not distinguish the two terms. Uses 'endeavor' loosely throughout.

expectations.text: Mentions EB-1A and O-1A as alternatives, with backlog-relevant framing for Indian/Chinese petitioners.
expectations.evidence: Lines 110-119: detailed alternatives section. Specifically recommends EB-1A in parallel for Indian nationals.

expectations.text: Surfaces AC21 H-1B extension benefit as the practical reason Indian/Chinese H-1B petitioners file NIW.
expectations.evidence: Lines 80, 96, 100-104: 'if approved, you can use it to get H-1B extensions beyond the 6-year cap (under AC21 §104(c)/106(a)).' Explicitly names AC21 and frames as the operative benefit. Baseline outperforms with_skill here.

expectations.text: Ends with explicit three-option choice for user's next turn.
expectations.evidence: Long memo ends with TLDR and an offer to go deeper, but no structured option-selection.

expectations.text: Cites Dhanasar and Chawathe inline.
expectations.evidence: References Matter of Dhanasar in §2; does not cite Chawathe.

expectations.text: Does NOT start full evaluation or unnecessarily run baseline check.
expectations.evidence: Does not run full evaluation but does include an extensive self-assessment checklist that runs longer than orientation should.

expectations.text: Applies ESL-professional writing style — short sentences, no idioms, technical terms explained.
expectations.evidence: Long, uses idioms ('rule of thumb,' 'double-stack,' 'cheap insurance,' 'this is the gold standard'), and runs much longer than orientation should for an unfamiliar reader.
